created_by: Spring (Forge job Oct 28; Ken approved both parts of take rotgut-grenadier-death in Oreheart Studio)
request: Goblin Chef (Rotgut Grenadier) (rotgut-grenadier): defeat animation from an owner-approved Runway reference video (front view, 6 s). refs/rotgut-grenadier--front.jpg is his model from the front; refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/fall-over/f01..f12.jpg is part 1 (0-3 s) and refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/lying-still/f01..f12.jpg is part 2 (3-6 s), 12 evenly spaced frames per part, time order. IGNORE in the video: the face, camera drift, and the small sideways shuffle of the feet at the very start (feet stay planted until he sits down). Owner rules for every goblin: nothing goes through his body, his held item or the ground; feet planted unless told otherwise (no sliding or sinking); weighty and cartoony, never floaty; poses read clearly from above and in front (board game camera). BASE POSE: these clips use "base_pose": "rest", so ctx.key turns are relative to the model's REST pose, the straight front-facing pose in refs/rotgut-grenadier--front.jpg. He faces straight forward (+Z, toward the camera) like the video. This is a rig motion reference only: never animate the face. FIRST Read all the pictures for a move, then match his BODY and LIMB poses frame by frame (torso lean and twist, head tilt, arm and leg angles, hip height) and the timing. If refs/ is missing or empty, do NOT write any animation files (the job will be retried). Do not touch, rename or remove any existing clip.

animations.name: OH_Death
animations.description: Death, from the owner-approved video: part 1 'fall-over' (refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/fall-over, f01-f12) then part 2 'lying-still' (refs/rotgut-grenadier-death/frames/lying-still). Frames 0-75 follow fall-over f01-f12 (frame N of 12 = about N*6 frames): from the base pose he wobbles as if very dizzy (small sway of hips and spine, head lolls), knees buckle, he sits straight down onto his bottom on the spot (about f09-f10), then tips gently backwards onto his back (f11-f12), legs up a little then down. Frames 75-90 he settles flat on his back like lying-still f01-f04 (small bounce, arms fall loosely out to the sides, legs relax). Frames 90-120 he lies completely still in that pose (no breathing). Use "move" on the hips to lower him to the floor: the hips go straight DOWN (and slightly back) to lying height so his body rests ON the floor, never under it. He stays in his own square: no sliding, no rolling away; his hips end within about 15% of his height of where they started. He keeps holding his big spatula the whole time (it stays in his hand and lies flat on the floor beside him at the end, never through the floor). This clip does NOT return to idle: key every bone you use at the last frame (120) with the lying pose so the clip ends lying down. LYING POSE, IMPORTANT (a first try sank his bottom 20% of his height under the floor): when he lies on his back (frames 75-120) the hips joint must end about 0.14 x ctx.height above the floor, NOT lower: with base_pose rest the hips start at about 0.36 x height, so key hips move=(0, -(hips_rest_height - 0.14*ctx.height), small backward offset) and no more. Lay him FLAT: hips turned back about 85-90 degrees ('right' axis), spine, chest and neck nearly straight in line with the hips (head resting on the floor, tilted a little), both legs lying along the floor (thighs turned so the legs are flat on the floor, knees only slightly bent, heels on the floor), arms resting on the floor at his sides. His back, bottom, heels and head touch the floor and NOTHING goes below the floor at any frame (the sit-down at frames 50-65 too: when he sits, his bottom rests at floor level, hips about 0.12-0.16 x height above the floor). Compute these heights from ctx.bones head positions before keying.

attachments.note: preview prop: his big spatula, held the whole clip
